confirmed.statement: The Study 1 statistics fit 48 per arm, but they cannot separate 95 from 96. The self-report t-test p = 0.016 reproduces from 48 vs 48 (t = 2.46, df = 94, p = 0.0157) and also from 47 vs 48 (p = 0.016). Partial eta squared 0.47 reproduces (0.466). F = 63.48 does not reproduce (62.30 with 146 poems and error df 143, 63.17 with df 145). This fits the form's flag that the printed df (145) does not match 146 poems.
confirmed.quote: A one-way ANOVA revealed that the creativity of the poems differed significantly across the three experimental groups, F(2, 145) = 63.48, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.47

confirmed.statement: Study 2 randomized and analyzed 152 people: 51 human, 50 human-AI, and 51 co-creator (51 + 50 + 51 = 152). No one failed the attention check. The form's n_randomized and n_analyzed (152; 51, 50, 51) match.

confirmed.statement: The paper states no sample overlap. Studies 1 and 2 are separate Prolific recruitments with different profiles (27.23 years and 76 percent female vs 35.11 years and 34.9 percent female). The paper does not say whether one person could join both, and the form's notes say so. Its one self-citation (ref. 59, a deceptive-chatbot study) is a different experiment. No other candidates.json record shares this task or the OSF project. The only shared author, De Cremer in c401, is on a separate 331-person marketing-campaign experiment. citations-family.json lists no sibling paper, and two web searches found no other paper that uses these samples.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds for each study on its own, and both studies randomly assign individuals. Study 1 analyzed 96 people (95 by the printed arithmetic), and Study 2 analyzed 152.
confirmed.quote: Condition assignments were random in both studies, with randomization administered via front-end programming.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Methods; PDF p. 2 and p. 4, 'randomly allocated to one of two/three experimental condition groups'

summary: The form's people counts match the paper: Study 1 analyzed 96 people (48 + 48, with the 50 AI-only poems kept out of every people count and the printed 101 - 6 = 95 gap flagged), and Study 2 randomized and analyzed 152 (51 + 50 + 51), sizes that reproduce all three printed F tests and the 34.9 percent female share. I found no wrong or unsupported count, no unreported attrition, and no sample shared with another paper, and each study on its own has more than 50 randomized people analyzed, so criterion 2 holds.
